m1.notes: M1 runs Ollama (qwen7b + ornith9b + nomic) + Java/Spring app. Java sees high CPU during build+inference overlap. Ollama RSS is modest (40MB) because GPU-offloaded models don't count toward process RSS.

hp.notes: HP runs qwen3b (small model, fast load) + Qdrant. HP is effectively maxed at 2 concurrent workers due to single-model constraint. Network latency to HP adds TTFT variance on cold arrivals.

bottlenecks.m1: GPU memory for 2 models (qwen7b + ornith9b). Adding 3rd worker causes queue contention.
bottlenecks.hp: Single model (qwen3b) limits to 2 useful concurrent workers. Network latency adds cold-TTFT penalty.
bottlenecks.network: LAN latency (HP) adds 5-18s TTFT variance on cold arrivals. Warm calls eliminate this.

utilization_assessment.m1_gpu: Well-utilized - 2 models loaded, 2 workers generating in parallel
utilization_assessment.hp_gpu: Modest - only qwen3b running, but this is the cheapest possible secondary model
utilization_assessment.network: Acceptable for LAN distribution - HP offloading reduces M1 queue pressure

optimization_opportunities.reason: HP only has qwen3b. Cannot run heavier models. Already maxed at 2 workers.
HP hardware limitations + network latency would not improve end-to-end throughput enough to justify. qwen3b is already the fastest viable secondary.

optimization_opportunities.notes: HP qwen3b is warmed before run starts. Eliminates cold-TTFT penalty on HP calls.

conclusion: M1 is the primary compute engine (2 models, 2 workers). HP is a useful secondary (1 model, 2 workers, RAG offload). The distributed topology is near-optimal for the current hardware. Further M1 utilization is blocked by GPU memory. Further HP utilization is blocked by model availability.
